title: Measured Twice
logline: In the weeks before the New Year, a tailor in a northern market town takes orders from a student who fears being looked down on, a mother dressing her children to impress, and a man who just wants a decent shirt.

object.note: Object 2 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: The same New Year season, far to the north: after the sweets, the new clothes, and the different reasons people give for wanting them.

thread_out.thread: The question of wanting to be seen passes from what people wear to what they give: an evening gathering place where the same stray dogs are fed for very different reasons.

requirements: An active tailoring shop with a season of orders
A tailor willing to be filmed working and talking with customers
Customers willing to explain their own reasons on camera

lesson.in_simple_terms: Two people can order the very same shirt for very different reasons. The texts say what makes it wanting is the reason inside, not the shirt.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: එකම ඇඳුම විවිධ අය මසා ගන්නේ විවිධ හේතු නිසා වන අතර, එය ආශාවක් වන්නේද නැද්ද යන්න තීරණය වන්නේ ඇඳුමෙන් නොව සිතේ අරමුණෙනි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma lists fine clothes among the everyday occasions on which greed-rooted minds (lobhamūla citta) arise, and then draws the line by motive rather than by act. Preparing and wearing clothes to look beautiful, to attract others or to seem superior is counted as greed-rooted, while wearing them to cover the body and keep off cold, heat and insects is not counted as unwholesome. Greed itself is described as the attaching that takes things to be good, beautiful or sweet.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The tailor's rhythm of measuring, chalking and stitching is the same for every customer, so the only thing that changes between orders is what each person says about why they want it. Hearing those reasons in the customers' own words, over identical chalk lines, the viewer is left to notice that the difference lies inside the person, not on the cloth.
lesson.caution: This does not mean that dressing well is wrong or that going without is a virtue: the texts do not preach deprivation, and the film does not rule on any customer's reasons.
lesson.builds_on: The last film showed feeling differing between people over the same sweet; this one shows the aim differing between people over the same act, and finds that the texts draw the line of wanting at the aim.
